reading.title: Ask the Weather Reporter
reading.purpose: Listen in as a student asks a weather expert how forecasts and weather words work.
paras: Zoe: Ms. Okafor, my class wants to know how you decide what to say in the weather report.
Ms. Okafor: I study clouds, wind, and temperature. Then I make a forecast, which is a report of what the weather will probably be. Notice that I say probably. Nobody can be sure.
Zoe: Last week there was only a drizzle, but I thought it would pour. Is a drizzle precipitation too?
Ms. Okafor: Yes. Precipitation is any water that falls from the clouds, such as rain, snow, or hail. A drizzle is just a very light rain with tiny drops. A gust of wind can blow it sideways, though.
Zoe: Why was the air so humid on Monday? My shirt stuck to me.
Ms. Okafor: When the sun warms a puddle or a lake, the water will evaporate and rise into the air. On some days, that leaves the air damp and sticky, which is what humid means.
Zoe: Does your job change in a place that is frigid or scorching?

Ms. Okafor: It does. The climate, meaning the usual weather over many years, is different everywhere. Some places are frigid in winter, and others are scorching in summer. In a place with a drought, I watch for any chance of rain, because people have gone a long time without it.
Zoe: Thank you! Now I can explain the weather to my whole class.

qs.q: In the last long answer, the word "climate" means
choices: the weather report for tomorrow in a single town
how much rain falls during one very big storm
the usual weather in a place over many years
the hottest and the coldest days of one year
qs.why: Ms. Okafor explains it right away: climate is "the usual weather over many years."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what a drizzle is?
choices: Precipitation is any water that falls from the clouds, such as rain, snow, or hail.
A drizzle is just a very light rain with tiny drops.
A gust of wind can blow it sideways, though.
Zoe: Last week there was only a drizzle, but I thought it would pour.
qs.why: This sentence names a drizzle and says it is a very light rain with tiny drops.

ev.text: A drizzle is just a very light rain with tiny drops.

qs.q: Why might a forecast turn out to be wrong sometimes?
choices: Reporters study only the clouds and never look at the wind or heat.
People forget the weather report before the next day arrives.
A forecast only works for places that are frigid or scorching.
A forecast says what will probably happen, so nobody can be sure.
qs.why: Ms. Okafor says a forecast tells what the weather will probably be, and that nobody can be sure.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this conversation?
choices: An expert explains forecasts, rain, and climate.
A student learns that the weather is the same in every place all year long.
A reporter tells why a drizzle is more dangerous than a thunderstorm in the spring.
A student decides to become a weather reporter after a rainy week at school.
qs.why: Zoe asks several questions, and Ms. Okafor answers each with a clear explanation about the weather.
